assessment: Eight tutors, one truth: they exist because your scarce class is two cards deep. Stack 001's census found eight mana-free sacrifice outlets and exactly one — Yawgmoth, Thran Physician — that also places a -1/-1 counter; the only other free repeatable source is Devoted Druid, and only while Mikaeus resets him. So the default wish from almost every tutor here is the same card, and that is a strength, not a rut: the goldfish has a tutor drawn in 78.0% of games, 67.6% by turn 6, mean turn 2.695, which makes a two-deep class play like a deep one. Know your delivery speeds. Demonic Tutor, Diabolic Intent, Grim Tutor and Survival of the Fittest put the wish in your hand now. Vampiric Tutor, Imperial Seal and Worldly Tutor put it on TOP — it arrives next draw, so those are appointments, not arrivals, and the instants fire at the end step before your turn to cut the transit time to zero. Green Sun's Zenith puts a green creature straight onto the battlefield — the only wish in the book that pays tempo instead of charging it. And one standing order: nothing in this section fetches on the promise of the Blowfly kill. That line is unverified. Fetch Blowfly Infestation as a counter source if the grind wants it — never as a two-card win.

targets.scenario: Turn 3. Hapatra landed on turn 2 — she does in 9,970 of 10,000 goldfish runs — a Snake or two in play, and nothing in hand that places counters repeatedly.
targets.why: The default wish for the whole book. Stack 001's census is unambiguous: of the eight mana-free sacrifice outlets, Yawgmoth is the only one that also places a -1/-1 counter. He is a Snake, a card and a removal ping per activation. Carry step 12's trap with you — one instance of 'target,' so keep a second body or the ability fizzles and you do not even draw.

targets.scenario: A free repeatable counter source is already online — Yawgmoth ticking, or the Druid loop live under Mikaeus — and three healthy life totals are the only problem left.
targets.why: The fastest converter you own. It drains each opponent on counter PLACEMENT, not on death, and stack 001 step 14 puts the Druid loop's steady state at four placements and one death per cycle — four table-wide drains per cycle instead of one. Zulaport Cutthroat is the backup; Blood Artist is a tier down because it drains one target player.

targets.scenario: You are behind. Two wide boards across the table, your engine half-built, real damage incoming.
targets.why: The behind fetch is the rebuild, not the reset. X counters on each creature triggers Hapatra once per creature, feeds Nest of Scarabs, and hands Necroskitter every opposing creature that dies with a counter on it. You come out of your own sweeper with a bigger board than you took into it.

tutors.notes: Two mana, any card, no strings. This is the tutor you never save for a clever turn — fire it at the first hole in the census.

targets.scenario: Turn 3 with Hapatra out and a spare Snake. Grim Haruspex or Blood Artist on board makes it sweeter.
targets.why: Intent's additional cost is a body — and your bodies are fodder whose deaths are triggers. Sacrifice the Snake, collect the death payoffs, take the one enabler the census says matters. Same wish as Demonic Tutor, nearly free here.

targets.scenario: Devoted Druid is on the battlefield and the table's creature removal has been counted and spent.
targets.why: The closing wish. Mikaeus + Devoted Druid is your one verified true two-card infinite (stack 001 steps 13-14): infinite deaths, placements, Snakes and drain — explicitly not mana. He costs six, and goldfish mean available mana is 6.150 on turn 6, so the cast lands on schedule the turn after the fetch.

targets.scenario: You are one untap from the pivot, and a single open answer would break the attempt.
targets.why: The one card that beats a targeted answer and a wrath in the same breath — hold it for the turn you go. One caution: whether hexproof and indestructible answers a -X/-X effect that kills by toughness is an open question that deserves its own stack scenario. Do not lean on it against Toxic Deluge effects.

targets.scenario: Turn 1, one green mana, an ordinary hand.
targets.why: X=1 is the turn-1 Zenith, and it turns your turn 2 into Hapatra plus a play. She lands turn 2 in 9,970 of 10,000 runs already — this wish lands her with company. Birds of Paradise is the alternate when the colours are awkward.

targets.scenario: Mikaeus, the Unhallowed is on the battlefield. Any table, any turn.
targets.why: X=2, straight onto the battlefield — and the verified loop needs no haste. The Druid's untap ability pays a -1/-1 counter as a cost with no tap symbol, so 302.6 never touches it; stack 001 shows three green on the first pass, zero after, and the deaths and Snakes running forever. Zenith is the only tutor that deploys the combo piece without a turn spent holding it.

targets.scenario: A counter engine is running and the board needs to become a clock.
targets.why: X=3 for the placement-speed drain — four drains per Druid cycle off stack 001 step 14's four placements, each one hitting every opponent. It is green, it is a creature, and most tables forget Zenith reaches it.

tutors.notes: Zenith shuffles itself back in — the deck's only reusable wish besides Survival. Spending it at X=1 early is fine; the deck can find it again.

targets.scenario: Turn 3-4, no counter source in hand, and the cheaper tutors are spent or absent.
targets.why: The same default wish with a 3-life surcharge — and the price is real in a deck already paying life to Yawgmoth, Bitterblossom, Phyrexian Reclamation and three painlands. Pay it for the enabler, never for a luxury.

targets.scenario: The engine is running, bodies are flowing, and your hand is empty.
targets.why: Every Snake, Insect, Faerie and Elf Warrior is a 1/1, so this is 'pay {1}, draw two' on repeat. When the board is ahead of the hand, the bodies-to-cards engine outvalues any single spell you could name instead.

targets.scenario: Turn 1 or 2, before the game has shape. Seal is sorcery-speed and the wish arrives on your next draw — it wants to be cast early, not at the pivot.
targets.why: Seal on turn 2 means Yawgmoth in hand on turn 3 and on the battlefield turn 4, on curve, for 2 life you barely feel that early. Fired late it telegraphs the pivot a full turn out and gifts the table a draw step to answer. Schedule it; do not spend it.

targets.scenario: A wrath is clearly coming — a control seat holds up mana, your board is wide, and your untap is the rebuild turn.
targets.why: Put the rebuild on top the night before. If the wrath comes, you untap into X counters on each creature — Hapatra triggers, Nest of Scarabs fills, Necroskitter collects. If it does not, you cast the table's best sweeper on your schedule instead of theirs.

targets.scenario: Any turn with {G} open and a spare creature card in hand — a dork whose job is done, a redundant body.
targets.why: The most powerful tutor in the list, and repeatable — the discard is barely a cost with Phyrexian Reclamation and Eternal Witness in the 99 to buy the card back. The first activation is always the census answer: the one free repeatable -1/-1 source.

targets.scenario: Late game, six-plus mana in sight, the table's removal counted and spent.
targets.why: Repeatable tutoring is what makes a three-card assembly realistic: Mikaeus this activation, Walking Ballista the next. That package plus any free outlet is verified genuinely unbounded (stack 001 step 15) — three cards, because Mikaeus's layer-7c anthem keeps a counterless Ballista alive at 1/1 and an external outlet is mandatory. Your eight free outlets are already everywhere.

targets.scenario: A creature table is going wide and you hold Black Sun's Zenith.
targets.why: The pairing that turns their board into yours — any creature an opponent controls that dies with a -1/-1 counter on it comes back under your control. Honest label: that read is oracle reasoning with no stack scenario behind it. Plan for it; do not promise it.

tutors.notes: Survival reveals each fetch. After the second activation the table knows exactly what you are assembling — budget protection or politics accordingly.

targets.scenario: End step of the opponent before you, turn 2-3, engine incomplete.
targets.why: Instant speed is the whole card: wish at the last legal moment and the top card is yours before anyone can respond to the draw — zero turns in transit. It costs 2 life and your draw step, so spend it on the turn the answer matters, not on curiosity.

targets.scenario: You are behind and next turn must be a reset — the aggro seat is lethal-adjacent and rebuilding is not enough.
targets.why: The pure panic button: -X/-X until end of turn, no counters placed, zero triggers for Hapatra, Nest or Necroskitter — sequence it as the emergency it is. Vampiric at their end step puts Deluge in hand for your main phase, and the X life comes out of the budget this deck already spends freely.

targets.scenario: A counter source is online, the pivot is next turn, and the kill needs a table-wide clock.
targets.why: Top it tonight, cast it tomorrow for three, and every counter placement drains each opponent from then on. On the Druid loop that is four drains per cycle (stack 001 step 14). The Spider draws far less heat on the stack than Mikaeus ever does.

targets.scenario: Turn 2, end of turn, one mana open, no counter source in hand.
targets.why: One mana at instant speed for the enabler on top — one draw away, so fire it the end step before your turn and the exposure is zero. The reveal is public: the table sees Yawgmoth coming, so expect the removal and keep the second body ready for step 12's fizzle trap.

targets.scenario: Mikaeus, the Unhallowed is on the battlefield with any free outlet — Ashnod's Altar, Viscera Seer, Carrion Feeder, take your pick of the eight.
targets.why: The verified closer: Mikaeus + Ballista + a free outlet is genuinely unbounded at 1 damage per iteration, no drain payoff needed (stack 001 step 15). Remember why it is three cards — the anthem keeps a counterless Ballista alive at 1/1, so the outlet does the recycling, not the Ballista itself.

targets.scenario: Targeted removal just clipped your enabler, and the tutor that found it is in the graveyard.
targets.why: The rebuy. Witness returns the tutor or the answered piece to hand on a body that is itself sacrifice fodder — two wishes for the price of one draw step, and the second one is private.

gaps: Every default wish is the same card, and the table learns that fast. Yawgmoth dies on sight anywhere competent — so plan the second fetch before the first resolves. Devoted Druid under Mikaeus is the verified backup engine, and Phyrexian Reclamation buys Yawgmoth back for {1}{B} and 2 life.

Vampiric Tutor, Imperial Seal and Worldly Tutor deliver to the top of the library — one draw away, and the wish can die in transit against held interaction. Fire the two instants at the end step before your turn to cut the exposure to zero, and treat the sorcery-speed Seal as an early-game card only.

No tutor in the 99 finds an artifact or enchantment answer, because none exists to find. Against a resolved prison piece the library has nothing — your outs are speed, politics and someone else's removal. The fetch quests make you faster; they cannot make you broader.

Nothing here fetches Blowfly Infestation as a kill. The line the goldfish tracks at 16.3% assembled is unverified — one of eleven unresolved entries. Fetch it as a counter source in a grind if you must; tap out for it as a win and you are betting the game on a line no checker has signed.
